Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5380 of 2023
Applicant :- Bhupendra Singh Yadav

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajai Kumar,Vivek Singh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri Ajay Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the records.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.116 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC & Section 66D of I.T. Act at Police Station- Kotwali Shahar, District Mirzapur with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, four co-accused persons, namely, Umesh Kumar, Deep Chand, Bhavar Singh and Satyam Singh Yadav, were arrested by the police involved in the racket of getting jobs to the persons through fake mark-sheets.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the Bhupendra Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92825787/
1 present case.

entities.text: Bhupendra Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has nothing to do with the said offence.
He is not named in the FIR.
His name has come up later on in the statement of arrested co-accused person which is not admissible under Indian Evidence Act.
Learned counsel has further stated that the investigation is going on and the charge-sheet has not yet been filed.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant has also stated that the applicant has co-operated in the investigation and undertakes that he will cooperate in the investigation in future also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of the anticipatory bail.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
6. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.
7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the applicant deserves to be granted anticipatory bail in connection with the aforesaid case.

9. In default or misuse of any of the conditions, the Public Prosecutor/ Investigating Officer/ first informant-complainant is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
